thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: Service=redwood-inference-api, Severity=high, IncidentID=PD-90234, Link=https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-90234

incident-bot: Auto-page fired to #incidents because error rate > 5% for 3m across eu-west1. Rule: api-5xx-spike.

alex: i'm on it, acked the PD page. grabbing logs and checking recent deploys.

maya: acked. i can help with query traces and the routing layer. any customer impact yet?

sam: seeing 502/504 spikes from the inference frontend -> runtime pool, metrics dashboard: http://grafana/redwood/d/llm-prod?panelId=7 :eyes:

ops_lead: good call. check if autoscaler recently scaled down GPUs in eu-west1. last deploy at 03:12 UTC?

alex: confirmed a scale-down event at 03:10 UTC and a tiny surge in *queue length* right after. pushing logs now.

maya: grep of runtime logs shows repeated `KVCacheMissError` on a subset of pods, stack traces attached. small percentage of requests falling back to CPU path.

sam: sample logs:
```
[2026-03-14T03:14:22Z] pod=inference-eu-3 level=error msg="KVCacheMissError" model=redwood-v1 req_id=0x7f3a
[2026-03-14T03:14:22Z] pod=inference-eu-3 level=warn msg="fallback to cpu-quant path"
```

nora: customers might see higher tail latency or 5xx. Can we triage impact: which routes affected? embeddings/tokens/generation?

alex: looks concentrated on /v1/generate for longer-context requests (>1024 tokens). embeddings unaffected.

ops_lead: mitigation plan: (1) pin traffic to alternative model shard (lower memory) for longer contexts, (2) temporarily increase pool size (burst), (3) enable aggressive prefix caching on edge. Which can we do fast?

maya: I can flip the routing weight to model-variant-b by hand (5 min). I'll also kick a forced scale-up of the Dedicated pool.

sam: if we change routing, add a slow rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% to avoid regression.

alex: doing 10% now. watching errors.

incident-bot: action logged: routing-change by maya at 03:18 UTC, rollout=10%.

sam: error rate dropped 30% within 60s after 10% shift. queue length starting to normalize.

alex: increasing rollout to 50% now.

nora: update for SRE/CS: initial impact window ~03:12-03:20 UTC, main symptom elevated 5xx on long generation calls in eu-west1. Customer-visible latencies up to ~15s and occasional 502s.

ops_lead: starting scale-up of Dedicated pool now (requested +2 GPUs). ETA ~4m.

maya: rollout at 50% holding, no new 5xx for last 90s.

pagerbot: :white_check_mark: PagerDuty PD-90234 acknowledged by alex, maya. Escalation paused.

sam: scale-up succeeded, new nodes registered to runtime at 03:23 UTC. metrics show KV miss rate back to baseline.

alex: promoting rollout to 100% at 03:24. monitoring.

nora: continuing to watch; opening a short post-incident note for CS with timeline. tagging impacted customers for transparency.

ops_lead: great work team. next steps: follow-up RCA to determine why autoscaler scaled down in presence of lingering KV footprint, and add smoother warm-up during scale-downs.

maya: filing RFC and assigning to eng-runtime for kernel warm cache handshake - will put preliminary notes in #eng-runtime.

alex: closing PD incident in 10m if stable. will hand off to day oncall for longer-term monitoring.

incident-bot: PD incident PD-90234 status=stable, last_alert=03:24 UTC.

nora: timeline for CS note:
- Impact start: 2026-03-14T03:12:00Z
- Mitigation: routing shift + pool scale-up (03:18-03:24 UTC)
- Impact end: ~03:24:30Z
- Customers: some longer-gen requests saw 5xx or elevated latency.

sam: +1 to adding a synthetic that mimics long-context traffic to catch this during scale events.

ops_lead: handoff: alex will follow up with on-call tomorrow morning; nora will draft customer outreach; eng-runtime to do RCA.

alex: acknowledged handoff. I'll create an incident jira and tag eng-runtime.

pagerbot: PD-90234: incident resolved, concluded at 03:34 UTC. :wave:
